text:
alex: taking over prim for the evening. I'm seeing pager for model-throttle-us-west -> grabbing the bridge now :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: model-throttle-us-west (P1->P2 recalculated). Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Estimated impact: elevated latency, ~8% error spike. Incident link: <https://incidents.redwood.com/INC-2026-472|INC-2026-472>
maya: i'm on it. quick check — are we seeing KV cache miss storm or autoscaler flapping?
sam: from metrics dashboard looks like kvcache eviction spiked after a large LRU purge at 20:12 UTC. Reqs queuing on inference pool.
jen: coverage note — i'm secondary but heads up i'm out at 21:15. If this escalates after that, alex you'll need to page infra oncall.
alex: ack. quick remediations I'm going to try: 1) check kvcache health 2) throttle burst clients 3) if needed warm a spare pool and redirect traffic.
maya: pointers/runbooks:
- KV cache stall runbook: <https://runbooks.redwood.com/kvcache-stall|kvcache-stall>
- Autoscaler runaway: <https://runbooks.redwood.com/autoscaler-throttle|autoscaler-throttle>
- Fast failover (warm pool): <https://runbooks.redwood.com/warm-pool-redirect|warm-pool-redirect>
sam: running quick probes:
```bash
# list inference pods with env tag
kubectl get pods -l app=inference,zone=us-west -o wide
# check kvcache metrics
curl -s 'http://metrics.internal/kvcache/us-west?window=5m' | jq '.'
```
sam: I see a shard with 95% eviction rate (pod inference-3). Plan: cordon that node, spin up warm pool c3, then move traffic.
alex: steps i'll perform now:
1) add rate-limit rule for clients/anonymous: /v1/generate to 10r/s (canary)
2) create warm pool c3 (scale up)
3) start a gradual redirect to c3
maya: +1. For the rate limit snippet use Kong route:
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "plugins": [{"name":"rate-limiting","config":{"second":10}}]
}
```
jen: FYI customer impact note: noticed a spike in 429s from a big customer (acme-corp). They are on dedicated capacity but fronting through the public pool for fallbacks. Might want to proactively message customer success.
alex: on it. I'll post to #support with initial blurb and hit the acme-corp CSM.
incident-bot: action log: alex added rate-limit rule at 20:18 UTC. sam started warm node creation at 20:19 UTC.
sam: warm node up -> readiness probes passing. shifting 10% traffic now.
maya: watching latency — p99 dropped from 2.2s -> 1.1s after shift. errors down to 2.3%.
jen: note for handoff — i'll be offline at 21:15, alex will be primary until 00:00. Secondary coverage fallback is maya until 22:30, then sam covers.
alex: handoff checklist for whoever takes over:
- check incident link and incident-bot timeline
- ensure warm pool health
- run kvcache diagnostic script in runbook
- customer impact update sent to #support
- escalate to infra if node boot failures >3
sam: quick command for kvcache diag:
```python
# run from ops machine
from redwood_ops.kv import Diagnostic
diag = Diagnostic('us-west')
diag.run_checks(['ttl', 'eviction_rate', 'hit_ratio'])
print(diag.summary())
```
maya: tagging runbook anchors below for next shift:
- Diagnostics anchor: <https://runbooks.redwood.com/kvcache-stall#diagnostics|diagnostics>
- Throttle scoring: <https://runbooks.redwood.com/autoscaler-throttle#scoring|throttle-scoring>
alex: thanks. I'll create a short postmortem stub after resolution. For now, keep monitoring. :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: pager resolved automatically at 20:45 UTC. Final state: warm-pool redirect handled 60% of traffic; system p99 restored. Closing notes saved to incident link.
jen: great. leaving final notes in handoff doc: <https://confluence.redwood.com/handovers/2026-07-15-evening|handover page>
alex: passing primary to maya for next 30m while i grab dinner — maya you ok to drive if anything pops?
maya: yep i got it. Good dinner alex. :plate_with_cutlery: 
sam: i logged commands and timestamps to the incident link. thumbs up.
